words.en: what does it mean; what's the meaning
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as shénme yìsi. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 这是什么意思. Hindari: saying 你什么意思？ with a sharp tone can sound confrontational.
words.when: Remember 什么意思 like the word you’ll use when a workplace word, decision, or message is still unclear — and you need the meaning before you act.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers ask 这是什么意思 / 这句话是什么意思 when a term or line is fuzzy. In formal settings, open with 不好意思 so it sounds like a clarification, not a challenge. Avoid a sharp 你什么意思？ — that can sound like you are accusing someone.

example.zh: 不好意思，这句话是什么意思？
example.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, zhè jù huà shì shénme yìsi?
example.en: Sorry — what does this sentence mean?

words.en: you mean; what you’re saying is
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as nǐ shì shuō. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 你是说……吗. Hindari: end with 吗 if you are still confirming; do not turn your guess into a definite statement.
words.when: Remember 你是说 like the word you’ll use in a meeting when you paraphrase someone’s point before you commit to action.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 你是说……吗 to check understanding: restate the ask, then wait for yes/no. Keep it as a confirmation question — if you drop 吗 and state your paraphrase as fact, you may lock in the wrong plan.

example.zh: 你是说，我们今天不用开会吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì shuō, wǒmen jīntiān búyòng kāihuì ma?
example.en: You mean we don’t need to meet today?

words.en: can or not; is it possible
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as néng bù néng. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 能不能再说一次. Hindari: do not treat it as the same as 可以吗, which often asks permission rather than ability/possibility.
words.when: Remember 能不能 like the word you’ll use when you need a natural workplace check on ability or feasibility — can this form be finished today, can they say it again.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 能不能 for possibility or capability in conversation (能不能完成, 能不能再说一次). Add 请 for more politeness. 可以吗 more often asks permission; use 能不能 when the real question is “is this doable?”

example.zh: 这个表格今天能不能完成？
example.pinyin: Zhège biǎogé jīntiān néng bù néng wánchéng?
example.en: Can this form be finished today?

words.en: say it again; repeat once more
words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as zài shuō yí biàn. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 请再说一遍. Hindari: 再 marks the next/repeat action; do not use 又 here.
words.when: Remember 再说一遍 like the word you’ll use when you missed a spoken instruction and need one clean repeat before you reply.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers soften the ask with 不好意思 / 请: 不好意思，你能再说一遍吗？ or 请再说一遍. Use 再 for “again / one more time”; 又 is the wrong marker in this request pattern.

example.zh: 不好意思，你能再说一遍吗？
example.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, nǐ néng zài shuō yí biàn ma?
example.en: Sorry — could you say that one more time?

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as màn yìdiǎn. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 说慢一点. Hindari: 说慢一点 asks for slower speech speed; 小声一点 asks for lower volume.
words.when: Remember 慢一点 like the word you’ll use when a colleague’s Mandarin is too fast and you need to catch — or jot down — the details.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers request 说慢一点 (可以说慢一点吗？) when speed is the problem. Do not confuse it with 小声一点, which is about volume, not tempo. Often paired with why you need it: 我想记下来.

example.zh: 可以说慢一点吗？我想记下来。
example.pinyin: Kěyǐ shuō màn yìdiǎn ma? Wǒ xiǎng jì xiàlái.
example.en: Could you speak a bit slower? I want to write it down.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as wǒ quèrèn yíxià. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 我再确认一下. Hindari: do not say 确认了 if you are only about to check; use 确认一下.
words.when: Remember 我确认一下 like the professional pause you’ll use when workplace details are not final and you need to verify before answering.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers signal a safe hold with 我确认一下 (+ time, numbers, owner), then 然后回复你. 确认一下 means you are checking now; 确认了 claims it is already confirmed — do not blur those.

example.zh: 我确认一下时间，然后回复你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ quèrèn yíxià shíjiān, ránhòu huífù nǐ.
example.en: I’ll confirm the time first, then get back to you.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as jùtǐ. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 具体时间. Hindari: 具体 is not a synonym for “correct”; it means a higher level of detail.
words.when: Remember 具体 like the word you’ll use when you need actionable workplace detail — date, place, number, or who owns the task.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers ask for 具体时间 / 具体一点 when vague plans cannot be executed yet. It raises specificity; it does not mean “right” or “true.” Pair with what you need: time, location, figures, owner.

example.en: Has the specific time been set?

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as bǐrú. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 比如说. Hindari: 比如 introduces an example; that example does not have to cover every case.
words.when: Remember 比如 like the word you’ll use when an abstract workplace idea needs one concrete example — especially when you lack words for a full definition.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers lead examples with 比如 / 比如说 to make an abstract point usable (比如改一下时间). One example illustrates; it is not a complete list of every case.

example.zh: 我们可以先做小调整，比如改一下时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ xiān zuò xiǎo tiáozhěng, bǐrú gǎi yíxià shíjiān.
example.en: We can make a small adjustment first — for example, change the time a bit.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as huàn jù huà shuō. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 换句话说，就是……. Hindari: do not use it to add a new topic; the phrase restates the same idea in simpler words.
words.when: Remember 换句话说 like the word you’ll use in a cross-team meeting when you restate the core message in simpler words so everyone shares one meaning.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers use 换句话说，就是…… to rephrase the same point more simply — useful across teams with different jargon. It is a restatement tool, not a way to sneak in a new agenda item.

example.zh: 换句话说，我们先试一周，再决定。
example.pinyin: Huàn jù huà shuō, wǒmen xiān shì yì zhōu, zài juédìng.
example.en: In other words, we’ll try for a week first, then decide.

words.note: Book headword pinyin printed as duì ma. Example-sentence pinyin not printed in the book; standard pinyin added. Pairing in book: 我理解得对吗. Hindari: 对吗 asks true/false; if there are several options, ask which choice explicitly.
words.when: Remember 对吗 like the short closer you’ll use after you summarize an instruction — check that your understanding matches before you execute.
words.usage: Most Chinese speakers tag 对吗 (or 我理解得对吗) after a paraphrase of roles, timing, or next steps. It seeks yes/no confirmation. When several options exist, name the options instead of a bare 对吗.

example.pinyin: Nǐ fùzé tōngzhī dàjiā, duì ma?
example.en: You’re responsible for notifying everyone, right?

notes.title: Module aim — fix miscommunication without freezing
notes.body: Modul 03 / Harian (book pages 12–14): repair miscommunication when the other person’s Mandarin is too fast or the meaning is still unclear. Indonesian title in the book: Minta klarifikasi tanpa malu. Soft openers (不好意思) keep clarification professional, not confrontational.

notes.title: Paraphrase before you act: 你是说……吗 / 对吗
notes.body: The book trains a safe loop: restate the ask with 你是说……吗, then close with 对吗 / 我理解得对吗 after you summarize. Keep 吗 when you are still confirming — do not turn your guess into a definite statement. 对吗 is true/false; if there are several options, ask the choice explicitly.

example.zh: 你是说，我们今天不用开会吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì shuō, wǒmen jīntiān búyòng kāihuì ma?
example.en: You mean we don’t need to meet today?

notes.title: 能不能 vs 可以吗
notes.body: From the book’s Hindari on 能不能: do not treat it as the same as 可以吗. 能不能 checks ability or feasibility in conversation; 可以吗 more often asks permission. Soften with 请 when needed (能不能再说一次).

example.zh: 这个表格今天能不能完成？
example.pinyin: Zhège biǎogé jīntiān néng bù néng wánchéng?
example.en: Can this form be finished today?

notes.title: Missed speech: 再说一遍 vs 慢一点
notes.body: 再不 marks a repeat (请再说一遍 / 你能再说一遍吗) — do not swap in 又. 慢一点 / 说慢一点 asks for slower speed so you can catch or note details; 小声一点 is volume, not tempo. Open with 不好意思 to keep both asks soft.

example.zh: 可以说慢一点吗？我想记下来。
example.pinyin: Kěyǐ shuō màn yìdiǎn ma? Wǒ xiǎng jì xiàlái.
example.en: Could you speak a bit slower? I want to write it down.

notes.title: 确认一下 is not 确认了
notes.body: 我确认一下 signals you are checking details before you answer — professional when information is not final. Do not say 确认了 if you are only about to verify; keep 确认一下 / 我再确认一下 until the check is done.

example.zh: 我确认一下时间，然后回复你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ quèrèn yíxià shíjiān, ránhòu huífù nǐ.
example.en: I’ll confirm the time first, then get back to you.

notes.title: 具体 / 比如 / 换句话说
notes.body: 具体 raises actionable detail (具体时间) — it is not a synonym for “correct.” 比如 / 比如说 introduces an illustrative example, not an exhaustive list. 换句话说 restates the same idea in simpler words for cross-team clarity; do not use it to add a new topic.

example.zh: 换句话说，我们先试一周，再决定。
example.pinyin: Huàn jù huà shuō, wǒmen xiān shì yì zhōu, zài juédìng.
example.en: In other words, we’ll try for a week first, then decide.

notes.title: Latihan 90 detik (book exercise)
notes.body: Book drill on p.14: pick three entries from this module — 什么意思, 慢一点, and 换句话说 — and build one work or daily story that uses all three. Record without reading the PDF, then check whether your timing and decisions came out clearly. No model Chinese dialogue is printed for this drill; do not invent one as book text.

example.zh: 什么意思 / 慢一点 / 换句话说
example.pinyin: shénme yìsi / màn yìdiǎn / huàn jù huà shuō
example.en: Target trio for the 90-second practice (instruction only; no sample story in the book).
